**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The exclusivity architecture in this Agreement runs entirely in our favour:

- **§ 5.8.1** — Harpoon and its Affiliates are barred from developing, commercializing or licensing any Competing Product in the Territory. This is exclusivity *granted to* AbbVie, which the playbook expressly treats as acceptable.
- **§ 5.8.2** — the Acquisition / Change-in-Control carve-outs still require the acquirer to Segregate the Competing Product and give AbbVie sole-discretion rights to cut off its Confidential Information flow and disband the JGC.
- **§ 5.1.3 / p0355–p0356** — the licences to AbbVie are exclusive, including as against Harpoon and its Affiliates.
- **§ 5.9.1** — third-party in-licensing restrictions bind Harpoon only.

No obligation binds AbbVie to source exclusively or to refrain from third-party procurement: **§ 4.5.1** gives AbbVie the *sole right*, not an obligation, to Manufacture (or have Manufactured) and supply, and the **§ 10.4** AbbVie covenants are confined to securing IP rights from its Affiliates, Sublicensees, employees and agents. Searches for "supply", "compet*", "neither Party shall" and "AbbVie shall not" surfaced no sourcing or non-compete covenant on us.

This satisfies the **preferred position** — no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on the Customer — so we recommend no change, and the Harpoon-side exclusivity should be preserved as drafted.
